paper.title: Family reunification and mental health

registers.role: linkage / sample frame: marital status, spouse and parental IDs used to match individuals to their spouse and children, and the spouse's 'first immigration year'
controls: annual income (entered in logs); the median income of the entire Danish population defines the income split
controls: highest observed education, grouped in 7 main categories
controls / sample split: employment status before family reunification
outcome: prescription data for mental illness (ATC codes N06 A, N05B, N05C, N05 A)

linkages: We match individuals to their spouse and children using the spouse and parental IDs in the BEF database.
Individual data is combined with information on a person's mental health status through prescription data for mental illness retrieved from LMDB.

sample.universe: First-generation non-Western immigrants living in Denmark, 1995-2019, who are registered as married and whose spouse arrives in Denmark (family reunification). Non-Western countries are all of Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, countries in North America (excluding Canada and the USA), countries in Oceania (excluding Australia and New Zealand), Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Russia, Serbia, Turkey, Ukraine.
sample.unit_of_observation: individual x event-time year (person-year in event time -2 to +5)
selection_rules: Consider only first-generation immigrants; Western immigrants are disregarded as there tends not to be any significant effect of family reunification on mental health
Only married couples can be identified, not cohabitants
For each married person, identify the year of arrival of the spouse; this is not the date of marriage

If the person is married before the spouse joins but the spouse ID is unobserved, assume the person is married to a spouse living outside Denmark, and take the earliest year from the spouse's 'first immigration year' variable
Keep all observations of immigrants observed in all the event-time periods from -2 to 5
The event study panel covers two periods prior to family reunification and five periods after, between 1995-2019
sample.n_individuals: 1830 non-Western immigrants (1280 men and 550 women in the main figure)

construction_notes: Education is measured as the highest observed education, grouped in 7 main categories: primary, lower secondary, upper secondary, short cycle tertiary, bachelor or equivalent, master or equivalent, and doctoral or equivalent
Income enters in logs; for observations with missing value, log income is set to zero (footnote 4)

Mental health is proxied by purchases of prescription medicine with ATC codes N06 A (antidepressants), N05B (anxiolytics), N05C (hypnotics and sedatives) and N05 A (antipsychotics), following Rouhe et al. (2011); the Fig. 6 robustness specification drops N05 A
The income split uses the median income of the entire Danish population in the year prior to family reunification
Employment split: unemployed in both of the two periods prior to family reunification versus employed in any of the two years prior
The event-time dummy at t-1 is omitted; all plotted coefficients are relative to one year before reunification

claims.statement: Five years after their spouse joins them in Denmark, non-Western male immigrants are less likely to purchase prescription medicine for mental health problems than one year before reunification.

treatment.label: family reunification (the partner joining their partner in Denmark)

register_source.value: BEF: spouse ID and the spouse's 'first immigration year' variable

definition.value: An event: the year the spouse of a married first-generation immigrant arrives in Denmark. Event time is measured relative to that year; the event dummy at t-1 is omitted, so each coefficient captures the effect of the partner joining their partner in Denmark relative to one year prior to reunification. For each married person the year of arrival of the spouse is identified; this is not the date of marriage.

timing.value: event time +5 years relative to the spouse's arrival (event year 0), measured against the omitted year t-1

outcome.label: medication use (purchase of prescription medicine for mental health problems)

register_source.value: LMDB: prescription records, ATC codes N06 A, N05B, N05C, N05 A

definition.value: A dummy taking the value 1 if the individual purchases any medicine for treating issues of mental health in event-time t. Medicine use refers to prescription to medicine with the following ATC codes: N06 A, N05B, N05C and N05 A. The codes are N06 A (antidepressant drugs), N05B (anxiolytic drugs), N05C (hypnotics and sedatives drugs) and N05 A (antipsychotic drugs), following Rouhe et al. (2011). Used as a proxy for mental health condition.

timing.value: measured annually in event time, from two years before to five years after the spouse's arrival

units.value: change in the probability of purchasing prescription medicine for mental health problems in a year (probability units on a 0-1 scale), relative to event time -1

estimand.target_population: married first-generation non-Western immigrants in Denmark whose spouse joined them through family reunification between 1995 and 2019 and who are observed from two years before to five years after that arrival: full sample of non-Western male immigrants
estimand.time_horizon: effect at event time +5 years after the spouse's arrival, relative to one year before (t-1); the paper considers a five-year horizon after the event

population.description: full sample of non-Western male immigrants; first-generation non-Western immigrants in Denmark, married, whose spouse joined them in Denmark
subgroups_defined: sex (estimated separately for non-Western male and non-Western female immigrants)
income above / below the median income of the entire Danish population in the year prior to reunification
job / no job before spouse arrival
reunification of children (none / at any time / along with the spouse)
country of origin exclusions (Turkey, former Yugoslavia, Middle Eastern countries)
population.selection: Kept only if observed in all event-time periods from -2 to 5 around the spouse's arrival; only married couples can be identified, not cohabitants; Western immigrants are disregarded

identification.source_of_variation: The timing of the spouse's arrival in Denmark under family reunification: for each married first-generation immigrant the year the spouse arrives defines event time 0, and outcomes are compared across event time within the reunified population, relative to the omitted year t-1. There is no never-reunified comparison group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Smoothness around the event time in the absence of the event: absent the spouse's arrival, the probability of purchasing mental-health medication would have evolved smoothly through the event window, so the event-time dummies relative to t-1 recover the effect of reunification.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors assert the assumption is credible in their case and ensures identification in the short run; the plotted event-study coefficient at t = -2 is close to zero in every panel.

key_assumptions.assumption: The five-year post-event window is short enough for the smoothness assumption to hold; identification over longer horizons would require further assumptions the paper does not make.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the method section; no test offered.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on being observed in every event-time period from -2 to 5 around the spouse's arrival (and on the couple being registered as married, since cohabitants cannot be identified); this selection is assumed not to distort the event-time profile.

implies_edges.from: observed in all event-time periods -2 to 5 around the spouse's arrival
implies_edges.to: purchase of prescription medicine for mental health problems (dummy)

key_assumptions.assumption: Purchases of prescription medicine with ATC codes N06 A, N05B, N05C and N05 A are a valid proxy for the mental health condition of immigrants.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Asserted with reference to Rouhe et al. (2011); the paper argues prescription data mitigate gender bias in self-reported mental health data.

key_assumptions.assumption: Where the spouse's ID is unobserved while the person is registered as married, the person is assumed married to a spouse living outside Denmark, and the spouse's arrival year is taken as the earliest 'first immigration year' recorded for the spouse.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Construction rule described in the data section (footnotes 2 and 3); no validation offered.

threats_discussed: Identification is argued to hold only in the short run; the authors say other identifying assumptions may be needed in the long run.
Only married couples can be identified, not cohabitants.
The spouse ID can appear in the registers some years after the actual arrival of the spouse, so the arrival year is taken from the spouse's 'first immigration year' variable.
robustness_checks: Excluding antipsychotic medicine (N05 A) from the outcome (Fig. 6)
Excluding individuals with Turkey as country of origin (Fig. 7(a))
Excluding individuals from Yugoslavia or any formerly Yugoslav nation (Fig. 7(b))
Excluding individuals from Middle Eastern countries (Fig. 7(c))

fixed_effects: dummies for age (non-parametric control for life-cycle effects)
dummies for years (non-parametric control for business-cycle effects)
controls: dummies for the highest individual education level
estimation.clustering: none reported; the figure notes state that standard errors are robust

source_table.value: Figure 2, panel 'Non-Western Male Immigrants', event time +5 (p. 3)

mediators_claimed: social support network system built by the first-mover migrant once the partner arrives

heterogeneity.finding: The decreasing trend in medication use gets stronger over time for non-Western male immigrants, while for non-Western female immigrants the improvement is significant only in year two and is temporary (Fig. 2, panel B).

heterogeneity.dimension: income (above / below the Danish median income in the year prior to reunification)
heterogeneity.finding: The general result is driven by low-income non-Western immigrants; there is no significant relationship for those with income above the population median (Fig. 3).
The improvement is very strong for non-Western male immigrants without a job before family reunification and absent for those with a job (Fig. 4).
Only family reunification without children is associated with improved mental health (Fig. 5).

The codes are N06 A (antidepressant drugs), N05B (anxiolytic drugs), N05C (hypnotics and sedatives drugs) and N05 A (antipsychotic drugs), following Rouhe et al. (2011). Used as a proxy for mental health condition.

timing.value: measured annually in event time, from two years before to five years after the spouse's arrival

units.value: change in the probability of purchasing prescription medicine for mental health problems in a year (probability units on a 0-1 scale), relative to event time -1

population.selection: Kept only if observed in all event-time periods from -2 to 5 around the spouse's arrival; only married couples can be identified, not cohabitants; Western immigrants are disregarded; individuals with a Middle Eastern country as country of origin are excluded

identification.source_of_variation: The timing of the spouse's arrival in Denmark under family reunification: for each married first-generation immigrant the year the spouse arrives defines event time 0, and outcomes are compared across event time within the reunified population, relative to the omitted year t-1. There is no never-reunified comparison group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Smoothness around the event time in the absence of the event: absent the spouse's arrival, the probability of purchasing mental-health medication would have evolved smoothly through the event window, so the event-time dummies relative to t-1 recover the effect of reunification.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors assert the assumption is credible in their case and ensures identification in the short run; the plotted event-study coefficient at t = -2 is close to zero in every panel.

key_assumptions.assumption: The five-year post-event window is short enough for the smoothness assumption to hold; identification over longer horizons would require further assumptions the paper does not make.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the method section; no test offered.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on being observed in every event-time period from -2 to 5 around the spouse's arrival (and on the couple being registered as married, since cohabitants cannot be identified); this selection is assumed not to distort the event-time profile.

key_assumptions.assumption: Purchases of prescription medicine with ATC codes N06 A, N05B, N05C and N05 A are a valid proxy for the mental health condition of immigrants.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Asserted with reference to Rouhe et al. (2011); the paper argues prescription data mitigate gender bias in self-reported mental health data.

key_assumptions.assumption: Where the spouse's ID is unobserved while the person is registered as married, the person is assumed married to a spouse living outside Denmark, and the spouse's arrival year is taken as the earliest 'first immigration year' recorded for the spouse.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Construction rule described in the data section (footnotes 2 and 3); no validation offered.

threats_discussed: Identification is argued to hold only in the short run; the authors say other identifying assumptions may be needed in the long run.

evidence.annotation: Medicine use refers to prescription to medicine with the following ATC codes: N06 A, N05B, N05C and N05 A. The figures include controls for income, Danish citizenship and education and non-parametric controls for age and year. Standard errors are robust. y-axis: “Medication Use Relative to Event Time -1”; x-axis: “Event Time (Years)”; panel title: “Non-Western Female Immigrants”; “Number of individuals: 477”

evidence.how: The paper prints no coefficient tables; the point estimate and the plotted interval were measured from the published figure at 600 dpi: the y-axis tick marks (.15 .1 .05 0 -.05 -.1 -.15 for Figs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7; .3 .2 .1 0 -.1 -.2 -.3 for Fig 4) were located in pixels and a linear pixel-to-value map fitted; the marker centre and the two whisker caps at event time +2 were then converted. Precision is about +/-0.002 in outcome units; the confidence level of the plotted bars is not stated anywhere in the paper.
